title: _totalWithdraw state-inconsistency: migration recorded as executed even when sharesToSell floors to 0 for a tiny-balance client (principal left on books, nothing moved)
description: _executeWithdrawal resets the two-phase WithdrawalState and emits WithdrawalExecuted BEFORE calling _totalWithdraw (correct CEI), but _totalWithdraw only zeroes clientBalances and decrements totalDeposited INSIDE `if (sharesToSell > 0)`. For a client whose live balance is a tiny fraction of totalDeposited, sharesToSell can floor to 0; the function returns having moved nothing and left principal on the books, yet the state machine is reset and the migration is recorded as executed.
impact: No fund loss — the un-migrated client retains full principal. Hazard is operational: the owner may believe a migration completed when nothing moved. State-handling / incorrect-as-to-operational-intent.
likelihood: Benign edge condition; tiny-balance client + sharesToSell rounding to zero.
assumptions: A client balance small enough that vault-share conversion floors to 0.
justification: NEW. C4 QA/Low: state-handling / incorrect-as-to-operational-intent, no asset impact. Distinct from H-02 (false-positive, run-11) — the cached-vs-live-read facet overlaps H-02's adjudication ('reading live balance is arguably more correct for a migration') and is NOT re-raised here; the PRIMARY false-migration-complete root cause is benign and novel. The cached-vs-live facet was routed by the faithfulness scanner as a documented quirk (no story-036 criterion pins to the snapshot), so this is NOT a faithfulness F — plain state-handling Low.
recommendation: Either revert / flag when sharesToSell floors to 0 with non-zero principal, or document that a sub-threshold balance is a no-op migration.
